elements.html: Please spend a few minutes exploring the tool before beginning the survey. Click the icon in your browser toolbar near the top-right corner of the browser window. Be sure to view all parts of the interface.

elements.name: A1_Q1
elements.title: Briefly describe (1-2 sentences), what do you think is the purpose of this tool?

elements.name: A1_Q2
elements.title: Please list the new information, if any, you learned by using this tool.

elements.name: A1_Q3
elements.title: Please list the information you already knew, if any, that the tool told you.

elements.name: A1_Q4
elements.title: Please list the surprising information, if any, that the tool told you.

elements.name: A1_Q5
elements.title: What questions, if any, do you have about what you saw in the tool?

elements.name: A6_Q1
elements.title: For each pair below, imagine you had to choose between Option A and Option B. Please indicate which you would choose.

rows.text: A: Free access to services, but your activity is stored indefinitely. B: A monthly fee, but no activity is stored.
A: Your activity is deleted automatically after three months, but recommendations get worse. B: Your activity is kept forever, and recommendations stay accurate.
A: Your search results are not personalized, but nothing you search is stored. B: Your results are personalized, but everything you search is stored.
A: A company decides which of your activity is sensitive. B: You label which of your activity is sensitive yourself, but must do it manually.

pages.name: A7
pages.title: Opinions about Activity Collection and Personalization

elements.name: A3_T1
elements.html: The following section repeats some of the questions you answered in the pre-usage part of this study. This is intentional: we would like to understand whether, and how, your opinions may have changed after using ADA for the past week. As before, during the rest of this survey, we use the term 'activity data' to refer to the records a company (e.g., Google) keeps of what you searched for, watched, visited, or did while using its services.

elements.name: A7_Q1
elements.title: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

rows.text: I would like the services I use to be personalized based on my past activity, as opposed to being the same for everyone.
I would be comfortable with a company keeping a record of what I search for and watch.
If it were available, I would like to use a system that shows me what activity data has been collected about me.
I feel that companies adequately explain what they keep in my activity history.
I feel that I understand how companies decide what to keep in my activity history.
I would consider it fair for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.
I would consider it creepy for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.

elements.name: A*_Q1
elements.title: What pieces of activity data do you think Google collects when you use your Google Account on multiple devices? (Select all that apply)
choices: Approximate location at the time of activity
Interactions with ads (e.g., ads viewed or clicked)
Data shared with third-party apps using Google login
elements.noneText: I don’t think Google collects data across services

elements.name: A8_Q2
elements.title: Imagine a regular Google user with a normal account, using Google services with the default settings. How likely or unlikely do you expect it is that Google retains a record of the following?

rows.text: The text of every search they have typed
Searches they typed but did not submit
Which YouTube videos they watched, and for how long
Voice recordings from Assistant queries
Places they physically travelled to
Their contact list
The colour of the device they used
Which apps they opened on an Android phone
Ads they clicked
Searches made while signed out
Searches made in Incognito mode
The content of their emails
Their Social Security / national ID number
How many devices they use
Purchases confirmed by email

elements.name: A8_Q3
elements.title: In the last week, about how many searches do you think you made on Google?

elements.name: A8_Q4
elements.title: In the last week, about how many YouTube videos do you think you watched?

elements.name: A8_Q5
elements.title: In the last week, about how many separate items do you think were added to your Google activity dashboard?

elements.name: A8_Q6
elements.title: Of the items in your Google activity history, about what percentage do you think are still stored from more than a year ago?
elements.description: 0% = none of them; 100% = all of them.

elements.name: A8_Q7
elements.title: Which of the following privacy approaches would you prefer for managing your Google activity data (e.g., searches, browsing history, app activity, YouTube history) in the future?
choices: Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data indefinitely, until I choose to delete it
Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data, but require Google to delete any data older than 3 months
Give consent to Google to collect and store all activity data, but require Google to delete any data older than 18 months
Store all activity data only on my device, allow required computations to run on-device, and share only aggregated results with Google instead of full data
Do not give consent to Google to collect or store any of my activity data, and delete any data currently stored by Google immediately

elements.name: A8_Q8
elements.title: Do you believe that Google ensures the security of the activity data it stores?

elements.name: A8_Q9
elements.title: On a scale of 1 to 5, with 1 being the least and 5 being the most, how much do you trust Google not to misuse your activity data?

elements.name: A8_Q10
elements.title: Do you think that you can access your activity data collected by Google?
